newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Azerbaijan president hints at new oil contracts.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan president hints at new oil contracts.

text.p: Azeri President Haydar Aliyev said Monday he might sign several oil contracts when he visits Washington later this week, but gave no details.
Answering questions at a news conference at the United Nations, he said Azerbaijan had signed six major oil contracts with multinational oil companies up to now.
"The companies are from the United States of America, from the United Kingdom, from France," he said, speaking through an interpreter.
"And also (companies) from Germany, Italy, Belgium, Turkey, Iran, Saudi Arabia and Japan are participating in the development of Azerbaijan's oil resources," he added.
"These contracts are being practically implemented," Aliyev said.
"We have also worked out several contracts. Maybe we will sign them during my visit to Washington. Wait two more days and you will get to know which contracts are they," he added.

Before Aliyev left Baku for his trip to the United States, Azeri officials said he would sign three contracts worth $10 billion with U.S. oil giants Exxon, Chevron and Mobil to develop three new offshore Caspian sea fields.

Aliyev told reporters before leaving that the nearly decade-old strife between Azerbaijan and Armenia over the region of Nagorno-Karabakh would be at the top of his agenda in talks with President Bill Clinton and U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
